standard_prerequisites.name: Normalization of a singular curve
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Varieties, Sections varieties-section-normalization and varieties-section-normalization-one-dimensional, with Lemma varieties-lemma-regular-functions-proper-variety
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the finite normalization nu : X' -> X, the finite extension k' = H^0(X', O_{X'}) and the short exact sequence 0 -> O_X -> nu_*O_{X'} -> Q -> 0 supported in finitely many points.

standard_prerequisites.name: Classification of genus 0 curves without H^0 correction
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies X' as P^1_{k'} once H^1(X', O_{X'}) = 0 and the conductor quotient is trivial on X'.

core_obligations: From the normalization sequence and finite support of Q (proof lines 2245-2262): H^1(X', O_{X'}) = 0 and 0 -> k -> k' -> H^0(X, Q) -> 0, so k'/k is a nontrivial finite extension of degree n.

Conductor ideal I = SheafHom(nu_*O_{X'}, O_X) with defining sequence 0 -> I -> O_X -> SheafHom(Q, Q) (proof lines 2265-2290); on an affine open U containing the support, the image of O_X(U) in End_k(V) is a commutative subalgebra of dimension <= n-1, giving 0 -> I -> O_X -> A -> 0 with dim H^0(X, A) <= n-1.

I is a nu_*O_{X'}-module, so I = nu_*I' (Morphisms, Lemma morphisms-lemma-affine-equivalence-modules); the cokernel A' fits into 0 -> A -> nu_*A' -> Q -> 0, whence dim H^0(X', A') <= 2n-2 (proof lines 2292-2310).

Divisibility (proof lines 2312-2325): H^0(X', A') is a k'-vector space, so its k-dimension is divisible by n; with A and A' nonzero this forces dim = n, i.e. I' is the ideal of a k'-rational point x', X' = P^1_{k'} by proposition-projective-line, and dim H^0(X, A) = 1 makes I the ideal of a k-rational point x; the skyscraper identifications A = k, A' = k' give the exact sequence 0 -> O_X -> nu_*O_{X'} -> k'/k -> 0.
proof_roadmap: Normalize X; read off genus 0 of X' and the extension 0 -> k -> k' -> H^0(X, Q) -> 0 from the finitely supported cokernel Q.
Introduce the conductor ideal and bound dim H^0(X, A) <= n-1 through the commutative-subalgebra argument.
Descend the conductor to X' as I', form A', and get the dimension estimate <= 2n-2.
Divisibility by n pins the dimension at n; conclude x', X' = P^1_{k'}, x, and the structure-sequence identification.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the explicit gluing diagram of a singular rational curve (statement lines 2221-2243). The proof (lines 2245-2330) turns the normalization sequence into a dimension statement through the conductor ideal: the bound dim H^0(X, A) <= n-1 from commutative subalgebras of End_k(V), the descent I = nu_*I', the combined estimate <= 2n-2, and the divisibility of dim H^0(X', A') by n = [k':k] which together force the conductor to be the ideal of a single rational point on each side. H3: the conductor bookkeeping and the divisibility pinch are a genuine argument, not a reference chase; the conclusion identifies the isomorphism type and the gluing data simultaneously.
